# Categorical plots

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

print("=== Creating Categorical Data ===\n")

np.random.seed(42)

# Create data with categories
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Player': np.repeat(['Aragorn', 'Legolas', 'Gimli', 'Gandalf'], 50),
    'Level': np.concatenate([
        np.random.normal(15, 3, 50),
        np.random.normal(18, 2, 50),
        np.random.normal(12, 2.5, 50),
        np.random.normal(50, 5, 50)
    ]),
    'Health': np.random.randint(30, 130, 200),
    'Class': np.random.choice(['Warrior', 'Mage', 'Rogue', 'Archer'], 200)
})

print(f"Data shape: {data.shape}")
print(data.head())

print("\n=== Bar Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.barplot(data=data, x='Player', y='Level')
plt.title('Average Level by Player')
plt.xlabel('Player')
plt.ylabel('Average Level')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Count Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.countplot(data=data, x='Class')
plt.title('Class Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Box Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.boxplot(data=data, x='Class', y='Level')
plt.title('Level Distribution by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Level')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Violin Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.violinplot(data=data, x='Class', y='Health')
plt.title('Health Distribution by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Health')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Swarm Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.swarmplot(data=data, x='Class', y='Health', hue='Class')
plt.title('Individual Health Points by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Health')
plt.legend().remove()
plt.show()

print("\n=== Point Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.pointplot(data=data, x='Class', y='Level', capsize=0.1)
plt.title('Mean Level with Confidence Intervals')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Mean Level')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Catplot (Faceted) ===\n")

sns.catplot(data=data, x='Class', y='Level', kind='box', col='Player', col_wrap=2)
plt.suptitle('Level Distribution by Class and Player', y=1.02)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Categorical Plot Summary ===\n")

print("Categorical plot types:")
print("  ✅ barplot: Aggregate statistics")
print("  ✅ countplot: Counts of categories")
print("  ✅ boxplot: Distribution summary")
print("  ✅ violinplot: Full distribution")
print("  ✅ swarmplot: Individual points")
print("  ✅ pointplot: Means with intervals")

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **Categorical plots compare groups.**

**Plot types:**

| Plot | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| `barplot` | Mean/aggregate by category |
| `countplot` | Count of each category |
| `boxplot` | Summary statistics |
| `violinplot` | Full distribution |
| `swarmplot` | All individual points |
| `pointplot` | Means with intervals |
| `catplot` | Faceted categorical plots |

**Basic usage:**
```python
# Bar plot
sns.barplot(data=df, x='category', y='value')

# Box plot
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='category', y='value')

# Violin plot
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='category', y='value')

# Swarm plot (points)
sns.swarmplot(data=df, x='category', y='value')

# Faceted plot
sns.catplot(data=df, x='category', y='value', kind='box', col='group')
```

**Python-chan says:**

# Overplotting with swarm plot

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Many points
np.random.seed(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Group': np.repeat(['A', 'B', 'C'], 500),
    'Value': np.concatenate([
        np.random.normal(0, 1, 500),
        np.random.normal(2, 1, 500),
        np.random.normal(-1, 1, 500)
    ])
})

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Swarm plot with many points (overlapping)
sns.swarmplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value')
plt.title('Swarm Plot - Too Many Points')
plt.show()

# Better: use violin or box plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value')
plt.title('Box Plot - Better for Many Points')
plt.show()

phase2.explanation:
**Swarm plots don't work well with many points!**

**What's wrong:**
1. 500 points per group
2. Overlapping points
3. Hard to see patterns

**The fix:**
```python
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Method 1: Use box plot
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value')

# Method 2: Use violin plot
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value')

# Method 3: Use box plot with swarm (sampled)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value', color='lightgray')
sns.swarmplot(data=df.sample(100), x='Group', y='Value', alpha=0.5)

# Method 4: Use strip plot with alpha
sns.stripplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value', alpha=0.2, jitter=True)

# Method 5: Use violin with inner points
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='Group', y='Value', inner='point', alpha=0.5)
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Swarm plots are for small datasets. Use box or violin plots for large datasets."
